config.title: Accordion

intro.title: Accordion
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple accordion component that allows users to expand and collapse sections of content individually. You will learn how to use Angular's built-in directives, such as *ngFor and *ngIf, to dynamically render and control the visibility of these sections. The core programming concept involves managing component state to track which accordion item is currently open. By the end, you will have a functional, interactive accordion using Angular and TypeScript.
intro.usecase: Accordions are a fundamental UI pattern used to manage content density and improve user experience by allowing sections to expand and collapse. In real software, you'll find them in FAQ pages, where questions are headers that reveal answers, and in settings panels of applications like Slack or Notion, where configuration options are grouped into collapsible categories. As a developer, you'll implement accordions in dashboards to toggle between data visualizations, in forms to reveal advanced options conditionally, and in navigation menus for mobile-responsive designs, ensuring clean, organized interfaces without overwhelming users.

objectives: Construct an Angular component with TypeScript to serve as the foundation for an accordion
Implement component state to control the expanded or collapsed state of each accordion item
Apply Angular event binding to toggle the visibility of accordion content on user interaction
Configure structural directives to conditionally render content based on the accordion state
Integrate CSS classes dynamically to visually indicate the expanded or collapsed state of accordion items
Manipulate component data to manage multiple accordion items within a single component instance
Initialize and bind component properties to pass data into the accordion for dynamic content display

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from Angular
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' at the top of your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path. Separate multiple imports with commas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular Component decorator and CommonModule are imported, enabling component creation and common directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one of the required modules. Make sure to import both Component and CommonModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the Accordion component class
steps.instruction: Create the AccordionComponent class with the @Component decorator and define its selector as 'app-accordion'.
steps.hint: Use the Component decorator imported in step 1 and define a class named AccordionComponent.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create the AccordionComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named AccordionComponent is defined with the @Component decorator and selector set to 'app-accordion'.
successCriteria: AccordionComponent class is created with @Component decorator and selector 'app-accordion'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined the class with @Component decorator and set the selector to 'app-accordion'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you've used @Component decorator and set the selector correctly.

steps.title: Define the accordion items data structure
steps.instruction: Inside the AccordionComponent class, define a TypeScript interface named AccordionItem with three properties: title (string), content (string), and isOpen (boolean).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a properly typed interface that describes the structure of each accordion item.
successCriteria: The AccordionItem interface is defined with title (string), content (string), and isOpen (boolean) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three properties (title, content, isOpen) are included with correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and define all three properties with proper types.

steps.title: Initialize the accordion items array
steps.instruction: Inside the AccordionComponent class, create and initialize an array property named 'items' that contains at least two accordion items matching your interface structure.
steps.hint: Define a public property with type AccordionItem[] and assign it an array of objects with 'title' and 'content' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an initialized 'items' array property ready to be displayed in the template.
successCriteria: The AccordionComponent class contains a public 'items' array property with at least two accordion item objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a public 'items' property with the correct type and at least two items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The accordion items array isn't properly initialized. Check that you've created a public 'items' property with type AccordionItem[] and assigned it an array of objects.

steps.title: Set up the component template structure
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a main container div with the class 'accordion' and use *ngFor to iterate through the accordion items.
steps.hint: Start with a div element and add the *ngFor directive to loop over the items array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a container div with an ngFor loop ready to display accordion items.
successCriteria: The template contains a div with class 'accordion' and an *ngFor directive that iterates over the items array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the container div with class 'accordion' and the *ngFor directive.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing. Add a div with class 'accordion' and use *ngFor to loop through the items.

steps.title: Add the accordion header section
steps.instruction: Inside the component template, add a button element for each accordion item in your items array. Use *ngFor to iterate over items and create a button for each one. The button should display the item's title and have a click event binding that calls the toggle method with the item's index.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let item of items; let i = index" to loop through items and access each item's title and index. Bind to the click event with (click)="toggle(i)".
steps.analogousExample: // Example: creating clickable list items
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a button for each accordion item with the item's title displayed and click event properly bound to toggle the item.
successCriteria: Template contains *ngFor loop iterating over items, buttons with (click)="toggle(i)" binding, and {{ item.title }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have: 1) *ngFor loop with index, 2) (click) event binding calling toggle(i), and 3) {{ item.title }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required button elements with click bindings. Remember to use *ngFor to create buttons for each item and bind the click event to toggle the item.

steps.title: Display the accordion item title
steps.instruction: Inside the header button in your template, use interpolation to display the current accordion item's title.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} with the item's title property inside the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying dynamic content in Angular
<button>{{ item.title }}</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion header button will show the dynamic title from the accordion items data.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation inside the header button that displays the item's title property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using double curly braces {{ }} with the item's title property inside the button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The title isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're using interpolation syntax with the correct property name.

steps.title: Add the accordion content section
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a <div> element for the content section that will be conditionally displayed when an accordion item is expanded. This div should be placed after the header section and contain a paragraph with the item's content.
steps.hint: Use the existing *ngFor loop structure and add the content div inside it. You'll need to access the current item's content property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: content section in a list item

{{ item.description }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a content section div that will display each accordion item's content text.
successCriteria: A <div> element for the content section is added inside the *ngFor loop, containing a paragraph that displays the item's content property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a content section, but make sure it's inside the *ngFor loop and displays the item's content property correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content section is missing or incorrectly placed. Add a <div> element inside the *ngFor loop that contains a paragraph showing the item's content.

steps.title: Display the accordion item content
steps.instruction: Inside the content section of each accordion item, add interpolation to display the item's content text.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the item.content property inside the content div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying dynamic content in Angular
{{ item.description }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion content section will show the content text from each item when rendered.
successCriteria: The content div contains interpolation binding to item.content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct property name 'content' from the item object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're using double curly braces with item.content inside the content div.

steps.title: Implement conditional display of content
steps.instruction: Add the *ngIf directive to the accordion content div to conditionally display it based on the item's expanded state.
steps.hint: Use *ngIf="item.expanded" on the <div class="accordion-content"> element to show it only when expanded is true.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: conditionally showing a message

This content is visible!
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion content div will only be displayed when the corresponding item's expanded property is true.
successCriteria: The *ngIf directive is added to the accordion-content div with the condition item.expanded.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added *ngIf="item.expanded" to the correct div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The *ngIf directive wasn't added correctly. Check that you're using the item.expanded property on the accordion-content div.

steps.title: Add visual indicators for open/closed state
steps.instruction: Add a CSS class binding to the accordion content div to conditionally apply a 'show' class when the item is expanded.
steps.hint: Use Angular's class binding syntax [class.class-name]="condition" on the <div class="accordion-content"> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion content div will have a conditional class binding that applies the 'show' class when the item's expanded property is true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct Angular class binding syntax [class.show]="item.expanded" on the accordion content div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a conditional class binding to the accordion content div. Review Angular's class binding syntax.
